title: Insurance claim fraud
ref: public knowledge: claim fraud detection practice
problem: Flag the motor claims most likely to be fraudulent so the investigation unit looks at them first.

understanding.unit: One claim at first notice of loss
understanding.target: The claim was later confirmed fraudulent by an investigator
understanding.moment: When the claim is filed, before any payment
understanding.labels: Only investigated claims have a verdict: most claims are unlabelled, not clean
understanding.action: Investigators review the top claims each week; a missed fraud is paid, a false alarm delays an honest customer

data: claims: date, policy, amount, injury flag, garage, witnesses
policies: start date, cover, past claims
parties: drivers, garages and lawyers shared between claims
pitfalls: Investigation outcome and payment amount are written after the moment: never features
Labels exist only where someone looked: positive-unlabelled, and the investigated set is biased toward what was already suspected
Rings share garages, phones and lawyers: a split by claim leaks the ring; split by time or by party group
Precision at the review capacity is the metric, not accuracy
solution: Rules and anomaly scores for the unlabelled claims, a classifier on the investigated ones, a graph of shared parties for rings
Split by filing date; report precision and recall at the weekly review capacity
workflow: Write the moment: what is known at first notice
Join parties and policies as of that date
Screen for leaks in the investigation and payment fields
Build the rules, the anomaly scores and the classifier
Compose on validation, read the holdout once at the review capacity

title: Credit default at application
problem: Score each loan application for the risk of default in the first year, to approve, price or decline it.

understanding.target: Ninety days past due within twelve months of disbursement
understanding.labels: Known only for approved loans: declined applicants have no outcome (reject inference)
understanding.action: Approve, price or decline; a default costs the principal, a wrong decline costs the margin

data: applications: income, employment, requested amount, purpose
bureau: history as of the application date
pitfalls: Bureau data must be as of the application date, not refreshed later
Only approved loans have outcomes: the model learns the old policy's population
A twelve-month window: the latest applications have no complete outcome yet and must be left out of training
Protected attributes and their proxies need a fairness review
solution: Out-of-time validation (the latest complete cohort as holdout)
Calibrated probabilities: pricing needs the rate, not only the rank
Monotone constraints where the business expects them
workflow: Define the outcome window and drop incomplete cohorts
Holdout on the latest complete cohort

title: Retail demand for replenishment
problem: Forecast next week's daily units per store and product so the replenishment system orders the right amount.

understanding.moment: Sunday evening, for the seven days ahead
understanding.labels: Sales are known for every past day; stock-outs hide true demand
understanding.action: Orders are placed from the forecast; too low empties shelves, too high wastes fresh stock

pitfalls: A day with zero stock shows zero sales, not zero demand: censored
Promotions are known ahead; weather is not (only its forecast)
A shuffled split puts the future in training: backtest at origins
Beat the seasonal naive (same weekday last week) before claiming a model
solution: Global gradient boosting over lags known at the origin, promotions and calendar
Rolling-origin backtests; the error scaled by the seasonal naive
workflow: Build lags only from the past

title: Predictive maintenance on industrial pumps
problem: Warn maintenance a day or two before a pump fails, from its sensors.

understanding.target: A failure within the next 48 hours
understanding.moment: At the end of each hour
understanding.labels: Failures from the maintenance log; planned stops are not failures
understanding.action: Schedule a check; a missed failure stops the line, a false alarm costs a technician's visit

data: maintenance log with failure and repair times
pitfalls: A window that reads past its end sees the failure
Rows are not incidents: count failures caught, how early, and alarms per pump-day
Pumps differ in their normal level: compare each to its own past
After a repair the series resets
solution: Features against each pump's own baseline (change, trend), a classifier on windows
Split by time and by pump; report failures caught and alarms per pump-day
workflow: Align the log and the sensors
Fit and choose the alarm threshold on validation

title: Churn of business subscribers (SaaS)
problem: Find the accounts likely to cancel at their next renewal, so customer success can step in.

understanding.unit: One account, ninety days before its renewal
understanding.moment: Ninety days before the renewal date
understanding.action: Customer success calls the accounts at risk; a call costs an hour

pitfalls: Usage after the moment (the last ninety days) is the future
Cancellation requests and refunds are written after the outcome
An account renews many times: group by account so its renewals do not cross the split
Accounts that churned early never reach a ninety-day snapshot: survivorship
solution: Snapshots at a fixed lead time, grouped by account, split by renewal date
Precision in the top accounts the team can call
workflow: Build one snapshot per renewal at the lead time
Features from usage before the snapshot

title: B2B lead scoring
problem: Rank new inbound leads by their chance to become a paying customer, so sales calls the best first.

understanding.target: Became a customer within six months
understanding.labels: Known after six months; recent leads are still open
understanding.action: Sales calls the top of the list each day

pitfalls: Sales activity after creation (calls, meetings) is the future and the treatment
Open leads are not negatives: drop or wait for the window
Leads from one company repeat: group by company
solution: A ranker evaluated by precision at the daily call capacity
Time split by creation date
workflow: Holdout on the latest closed cohort

title: Support ticket triage
problem: Route each new ticket to the right team and flag the urgent ones from its text and form fields.

understanding.target: The team that resolved it; urgent or not
understanding.labels: The resolving team for every closed ticket
understanding.action: The ticket goes to the team's queue; a wrong route costs a transfer

pitfalls: Resolver, resolution time and closing notes are written after the moment
Tiny teams: macro metrics and stratified folds
Duplicate submissions cross the split
Text embeddings must be fitted on training tickets only
solution: Text with tabular fields; macro F1 and per-team recall
Group by customer to test generalisation
workflow: Encode the text on training folds

title: Delivery time estimate (ETA)
problem: Tell the customer at checkout how many minutes their order will take.

understanding.moment: At checkout, before a courier is assigned
understanding.labels: Every delivered order; cancelled ones have none
understanding.action: The promise shown to the customer; late orders cost refunds

data: order time, distance, restaurant, basket size
pitfalls: Delivered-at minus ordered-at is the target: any timestamp after checkout leaks it
Times above a cap are stored as the cap: censored
Restaurants differ: group by restaurant for new ones
Quantile error matters more than the mean for a promise
solution: Gradient boosting with a quantile loss for the promise
Time split; report MAE and the share of late promises

title: Ride price acceptance
problem: Predict whether a rider accepts the quoted price, to choose the price that balances acceptance and margin.

understanding.action: The price shown; a price too high loses the ride, too low loses margin

data: supply and demand at the moment
pitfalls: Acceptance time and the final fare are after the moment
Past prices were chosen by the old policy: the effect of price is confounded
A random experiment on price is worth more than any observational model
solution: A calibrated acceptance model; price effects only from randomised quotes or careful causal design
workflow: Separate the policy's choices from the effect

title: Product recommendations for a webshop
problem: Show each visitor a personal top ten of products they are likely to buy next.

understanding.target: The products bought in the next 14 days
understanding.moment: At the date of the recommendation
understanding.action: The top ten shown; a good list raises sales

pitfalls: A random split leaks the future: split by time
Popularity is a strong baseline that must be beaten
New products and new customers have no history (cold start)
solution: Recall and NDCG at ten on the next period, against popularity and recent-items baselines

title: Who to send a discount to (uplift)
problem: Send the voucher only to customers whose buying it changes, not to those who would buy anyway.

understanding.target: Bought within 30 days, with and without the voucher
understanding.labels: A random holdout group without the voucher
understanding.action: Send or not; a voucher to a sure buyer is wasted margin

pitfalls: Without a random control there is no uplift to learn
A response model ranks the sure buyers first: the wrong target
Evaluate with uplift curves (Qini), not accuracy
solution: Two-model or transformed-outcome learners on the randomised campaign
Qini on a holdout of the campaign

title: Unusual card payments without labels
problem: Surface the strangest payments of the day for an analyst, before any fraud is confirmed.

understanding.labels: None, or a few confirmed cases later
understanding.action: An analyst reviews the top list; their verdicts become labels

data: payments with merchant, amount, country, device
pitfalls: Unusual is not fraud: measure on planted or confirmed cases
Compare a payment to its card's own past, not to everyone
Feedback loops: the analysts only see what the detector shows
solution: Detectors chosen on planted anomalies of a validation period
A review list of the analyst's capacity; confirmed alerts become labels for a classifier later

title: Hospital readmission within 30 days
problem: At discharge, flag the patients most likely to come back within 30 days, for a follow-up call.

understanding.labels: Known 30 days later; transfers and deaths need rules
understanding.action: A nurse calls the flagged patients; a missed readmission costs a bed

pitfalls: Codes billed after discharge are the future
Patients repeat: group by patient
Death within 30 days is not a non-readmission
Sensitive data: names and identifiers never leave
solution: Grouped time split; calibrated risk; recall at the nurses' capacity
A fairness review across patient groups
workflow: Define the outcome with its exceptions

title: Electricity load forecast
problem: Forecast tomorrow's hourly load for each substation, for the dispatch plan.

understanding.action: Generation is scheduled from it; errors cost balancing energy

pitfalls: Use the temperature forecast available at 10:00, not the measured temperature
Daylight saving days have 23 or 25 hours
Holidays behave like Sundays
solution: Gradient boosting on lags at the origin, forecast weather and calendar, backtests at many origins

title: Employee attrition
problem: Estimate which employees may leave in the next six months, to plan retention conversations.

understanding.unit: One employee at a quarter's start
understanding.action: Managers hold a conversation; it must never be used to punish

pitfalls: Exit interviews and resignation dates are after the moment
Censoring: people still employed are not 'stayed forever'
Small teams: identifiable people; aggregate what is shown
Ethics: an advisory signal, never a decision
solution: A survival model or snapshots with a fixed window; report on the latest quarter

title: Revenue of a new store location
problem: Estimate yearly revenue of a candidate site before opening a store there.

understanding.action: Open or not; a bad site loses the fit-out

data: footfall, population and competitors around each site
pitfalls: Neighbouring stores share demand: a random split leaks the area; split by spatial blocks
Revenue after year one reflects the store's own success
Few stores: wide intervals
solution: Spatial-block cross-validation; intervals, not only a point estimate
